The Insurance Company aggrieved by the award passed by the learned III Additional District Judge,
Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Villupuram @ Kallakurichi in M.C.O.P.No.417 of 2018 on 27.10.2021, has filed he present appeal questioning the liability mulcted upon the Insurance Company.

III Additional District Judge,
Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Villupuram @ Kallakurichi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2.The respondents 1 to 3 / claimants are the wife, son and mother of the deceased Ramar.
The case of the claimants is that the deceased Ramar was traveling as a loadman in the vehicle belonging to 4th respondent herein.
It is alleged that the vehicle was driven in a rash and negligent manner and as a result, it capsized and the deceased sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the injuries.
It is under these circumstances, the claim petition came to be filed before the Tribunal seeking for payment of compensation.

3.The Tribunal on considering the facts and circumstances of the case and on appreciation of oral and documentary evidence, came to a conclusion that the deceased was working as a loadman and w a s e m p l o y e d b y t h e 4 t h r e s p o n d e n t a n d t h a t t h e d r i v e r o f t h e v e h i c l e h a d https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis driven the Tata Ace vehicle in a rash and negligent manner causing the accident.
Having rendered such a finding, the Tribunal proceeded to fix the compensation under various heads and the total compensation was fixed at Rs.12,30,000/-.
This amount was directed to be paid with 7.5% interest.
4.Aggrieved by the above award passed by the Tribunal, the Insurance Company has filed the present appeal.
5.Heard the learned counsel for the appellant.
6.The respondents have served with notice and their names have also been printed in the cause list.
There is no representation either in person or through counsel.
7.This Court has carefully considered the submissions made by the learned counsel for the appellant and carefully went through the award passed by the Tribunal.
8 . T h e s p e c i f i c c a s e o f t h e c l a i m a n t s i s t h a t t h e d e c e a s e d R a m a r w a s https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis working as a loadman with 4th respondent.
Thus, the plea of employer / employee was raised.
The claim petition that was filed before the Tribunal shows that the 4th respondent was not shown as the employer in this case.
That apart, in the FIR that was registered pursuant to the accident which was marked as Ex.P1, it has been stated as follows:

11.In so far as the gratuitous passenger is concerned, the law on the issue is now settled by the Full Bench of this Court in 2009 (1) CTC 1, [Branch Manager, United India Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs.
Nagammal and 2 others].

entities.text:
2009 (1) CTC 1, [Branch Manager, United India Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs.
Nagammal and 2 others]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The Full Bench has clarified that in the event of passengers traveling in the goods vehicle whether gratuitous or otherwise, are not covered and any award passed after Baljith Kaur case reported in 2004 (1) TNMAC 1, [National Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Baljit Kaur &
others], the doctrine of pay and recovery cannot apply.

entities.text:
2004 (1) TNMAC 1, [National Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Baljit Kaur &
others]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This position of law has been followed consistently by this Court till date.
12.In the light of the above discussion, there is no question of directing the Insurance Company to pay the compensation to the claimants.

However, it is made clear that the compensation fixed by the Tribunal is liable to be paid by the owner of the vehicle, who is the 4th respondent herein and the claimants can proceed against him in the https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis manner known to law.
13.In the result

, the award passed by the learned III Additional District Judge, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Villupuram @ Kallakurichi in M.C.O.P.No.417 of 2018 on 27.10.2021 is set aside to the extent of fixing the liability on the Insurance Company and the liability can only be fastened as against the owner of the vehicle, namely the 4th respondent in this appeal.
